questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Definite Integral Using Multiple Properties of Definite Integrals
questions.problem: Suppose that $f(x)$ is a  function such that ${\int }_{2}^{-2}\frac{1}{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x=-3$ and ${\int }_{2}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x=10.$  What is the value of ${\int }_{-2}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x?$
questions.worked_solution:
Let's simplify one of the given integrals:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{2}^{-2}\frac{1}{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-3 \\ \frac{1}{4}{\int }_{2}^{-2}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-3 \\ -\frac{1}{4}{\int }_{-2}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-3 \\ {\int }_{-2}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =12\end{aligned}
$$

Then, from the adjacent intervals rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-2}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-2}^{2}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{2}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =12+10 \\  & =22.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating an Integral Given Another Integral With Reversed Limits of Integration
questions.worked_solution:
Let's reverse the limits of integration on the known result:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{6}\,f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{\int }_{6}^{0}\,f(x)\,\text{d}x=-4\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can split up the given integral using the sum rule and factor out the constants. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{6}(5f(x)+1)\,\text{d}x & =5{\int }_{0}^{6}f(x)\,\text{d}x\,+\,{\int }_{0}^{6}\,\text{d}x \\  & =5(-4)\,+\,x\,{|}_{0}^{6} \\  & =-20\,+\,(6-0) \\  & =-20\,+\,6 \\  & =-14.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating an Integral Given Another Integral With Reversed Limits of Integration
questions.worked_solution:
Let's reverse the limits of integration on the known result:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{4}\,f(x)\,\text{d}x=-{\int }_{4}^{1}\,f(x)\,\text{d}x=3\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can split up the given integral using the sum rule and factor out the constants. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{4}(2f(x)+x)\,\text{d}x & =2{\int }_{1}^{4}f(x)\,\text{d}x\,+\,{\int }_{1}^{4}x\,\text{d}x \\  & =2(3)\,+\,\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}\,{|}_{1}^{4} \\  & =6\,+\,\frac{16-1}{2} \\  & =6\,+\,\frac{15}{2} \\  & =\frac{27}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Definite Integral Given Integrals Over Adjacent Intervals
questions.worked_solution:
From the adjacent intervals rule, we know that

$$
{\int }_{3}^{7}f(x)\,\text{d}x\,+\,{\int }_{7}^{10}f(x)\,\text{d}x\,=\,{\int }_{3}^{10}f(x)\,\text{d}x.
$$

Plugging in the known information gives

$$
0+5\,=\,{\int }_{3}^{10}f(x)\,\text{d}x\,⇒\,{\int }_{3}^{10}f(x)\,\text{d}x=5.
$$

Finally, compute the desired integral:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{3}^{10}(3f(x)-4)\,\text{d}x & =3{\int }_{3}^{10}f(x)\,\text{d}x\,-\,4{\int }_{3}^{10}1\,\text{d}x \\  & =3(5)\,-\,4\cdot x{|}_{3}^{10} \\  & =15\,-\,4(10-3) \\  & =15-28 \\  & =-13\end{aligned}
$$

questions.knowledge_point: Evaluating a Definite Integral Using Multiple Properties of Definite Integrals
questions.worked_solution:
Let's simplify one of the given integrals:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{5}^{-1}7\,f(x)\,\text{d}x & =14 \\ 7{\int }_{5}^{-1}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =14 \\ -7{\int }_{-1}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =14 \\ {\int }_{-1}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Then, from the adjacent intervals rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-4}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x & ={\int }_{-4}^{-1}f(x)\,\text{d}x+{\int }_{-1}^{5}f(x)\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}+(-2) \\  & =-\frac{3}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
